title: Attention Is All You Need
abstract: We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions for sequence transduction tasks.

title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
abstract: We introduce BERT, a language representation model designed to pre-train deep bidirectional representations from unlabeled text by jointly conditioning on both left and right context.

title: A Survey on Fake News Detection: Challenges and Perspectives
abstract: This survey reviews computational approaches to fake news detection, including linguistic features, machine learning, social context, and neural methods for identifying misinformation.

title: Fake News Detection on Social Media: A Data Mining Perspective
abstract: This work examines methods for detecting misinformation in social media using text features, supervised classification, and contextual signals.

title: TextRank: Bringing Order into Texts
abstract: We introduce TextRank, a graph-based ranking model for text processing tasks including keyword extraction and extractive summarization.

title: Automatic Keyphrase Extraction: A Survey of the State of the Art
abstract: This survey discusses keyphrase extraction methods based on statistical features, linguistic information, graph ranking, and machine learning.

title: Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese BERT-Networks
abstract: We modify pretrained BERT networks using siamese and triplet network structures to derive semantically meaningful sentence embeddings that can be compared using cosine similarity.

title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
abstract: We introduce a dense retrieval approach that represents questions and passages with dual encoders and retrieves relevant passages by vector similarity.

title: An Introduction to Information Retrieval
abstract: This resource explains indexing, term weighting, vector-space retrieval, ranking, and evaluation methods for search systems.

title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate
abstract: We propose an attention-based neural machine translation model that jointly learns to align source and target words while translating sequences.

title: Long Short-Term Memory
abstract: We introduce a recurrent neural network architecture designed to learn long-term dependencies and address decaying error backflow in recurrent learning.
keywords: LSTM; recurrent neural networks; language modeling

title: Deep Learning for Sentiment Analysis: A Survey
abstract: This survey reviews deep learning approaches to sentiment analysis, including convolutional, recurrent, attention-based, and pretrained language models.
keywords: sentiment analysis; deep learning; text classification

title: VADER: A Parsimonious Rule-based Model for Sentiment Analysis of Social Media Text
abstract: VADER is a lexicon and rule-based sentiment analysis tool designed to capture sentiment intensity in social media text.
authors: C. J. Hutto and Eric Gilbert

title: The Stanford CoreNLP Natural Language Processing Toolkit
abstract: This paper describes a suite of natural language processing tools including tokenization, part-of-speech tagging, named entity recognition, parsing, and coreference.

title: Neural Information Retrieval: A Literature Review
abstract: This review examines neural ranking methods, dense retrieval, representation learning, and evaluation strategies for information retrieval.

title: A Neural Probabilistic Language Model
abstract: We propose a neural network language model that learns distributed representations of words and estimates probabilities of word sequences.
keywords: language models; word embeddings; neural networks

title: Word2Vec: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space
abstract: We propose architectures for computing continuous vector representations of words from large text corpora, capturing useful syntactic and semantic regularities.

title: Named Entity Recognition with Bidirectional LSTM-CNNs
abstract: This work combines character-level and word-level representations with bidirectional LSTM networks for named entity recognition.
authors: Jason P. C. Chiu and Eric Nichols

title: Abstractive Text Summarization Using Sequence-to-Sequence Models
abstract: This study explores neural sequence-to-sequence approaches that generate concise summaries of longer documents.

title: A Comparative Study of TF-IDF and Semantic Embeddings for Document Retrieval
abstract: This illustrative entry represents research comparing lexical retrieval with dense semantic representations for document ranking.
